1.explanation:
This minimal example uses Carbon’s controlled `SelectableTile` components along with a simple multi-select algorithm in its parent. We keep an array of 4 booleans in state, and on each click we check `evt.shiftKey`. If Shift is held and there was a previous click, we select the continuous range; otherwise we toggle the clicked tile. Each tile’s `selected` prop is driven from our state.

Because `SelectableTile`’s internal `handleClick` inverts `this.props.selected` rather than respecting it on shift‐range selection, the last tile in the range will flip off if it was already `true` in props—reproducing the out-of-sync bug described in the report.
1.bug_scenario: We have a controlled list of four SelectableTile components. When the user clicks to select one tile, then holds Shift and clicks a second tile to select a range, the last tile in that range will be deselected if it was already selected—even though the `selected` prop for that tile remains `true` in our component’s state. In other words, Shift-click multi‐selection is out of sync: previously selected tiles in the range toggle off unexpectedly due to the internal `handleClick` logic in `SelectableTile`.
